metadata.title: A finite volume scheme for convection-diffusion equations with nonlinear diffusion derived from the Scharfetter-Gummel scheme

extraction_notes.note: Hypotheses (H1)-(H5) are items of one sentence in a description list; since nodes never split a sentence, they form one assumption node rather than five.

The convergence-order tables and the figures of Sections 1.3 and 5 are not nodes; only the prose conclusions drawn from them are kept as numerical remarks. Several purely descriptive comparison sentences in the Motivation are left out.
The remark states and proves that the extended flux vanishes at discrete equilibrium; its assertion is a nested claim and its 'Indeed' argument a proof.
The conclusion cites the continuous estimate as (\ref{H}), which labels the definition of H; the intended reference is probably (\ref{inegentropie}).
Remark states an L-infinity result for the drift-diffusion scheme justified only by reference to a cited proof; kept as a remark with rigor semi_formal rather than a proposition.

nodes.statement: The drift-diffusion system consists of two continuity equations for the electron density $N(x,t)$ and the hole density $P(x,t)$, as well as a Poisson equation for the electrostatic potential $V(x,t)$, for $t \in \mathbb{R}^{+}$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}^{d}$.

nodes.name: Power-law pressure
nodes.statement: The pressure has the form of a power law, \begin{equation*} r(s)=s^{\gamma}, \quad \gamma \geq 1. \end{equation*}

nodes.statement: We supplement these equations with initial conditions $N_{0}(x)$ and $P_{0}(x)$ and physically motivated boundary conditions: the boundary $\Gamma=\partial \Omega$ is split into two parts $\Gamma=\Gamma^{D} \cup \Gamma^{N}$ and the boundary conditions are Dirichlet boundary conditions $ \overline{N}$, $ \overline{P}$ and $ \overline{V}$ on ohmic contacts $\Gamma^{D}$ and homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions on $r(N)$, $r(P)$ and $V$ on insulating boundary segments $\Gamma^{N}$.
nodes.statement_short: Initial data and mixed boundary conditions: Dirichlet on ohmic contacts, homogeneous Neumann on insulating segments.

nodes.name: Convergence to thermal equilibrium for the drift-diffusion system (Juengel)
nodes.statement: It is proved that the solution to the transient system converges to a solution of the thermal equilibrium state as $t \rightarrow \infty$ if the Dirichlet boundary conditions are in thermal equilibrium.
assumptions: the Dirichlet boundary conditions are in thermal equilibrium
conclusions: the solution to the transient system converges to a solution of the thermal equilibrium state as $t \rightarrow \infty$

nodes.name: Enthalpy function and its generalized inverse
nodes.statement: We introduce the enthalpy function $h$ defined by \begin{equation} h(s)=\int_{1}^{s}\frac{r'(\tau)}{\tau}\, d\tau \end{equation} and the generalized inverse $g$ of $h$ defined by \begin{equation*} g(s)=\left\{ \begin{array}{rcl} h^{-1}(s) &\text{ if }& h(0^{+})<s<\infty,\\ 0 &\text{ if }& s \leq h(0^{+}).\end{array}\right. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Enthalpy function h
nodes.statement: h(s)=\int_{1}^{s}\frac{r'(\tau)}{\tau}\, d\tau
nodes.label: h

nodes.name: Thermal equilibrium state (N^eq, P^eq, V^eq)
nodes.statement: If the boundary conditions satisfy $\overline{N},\overline{P}>0$ and \begin{equation*} h(\overline{N})-\overline{V}=\alpha_{N} \text{ and } h(\overline{P})+\overline{V}=\alpha_{P} \text{ on } \Gamma^{D}, \end{equation*} the thermal equilibrium is defined by \begin{equation} N^{eq}(x)=g\left(\alpha_{N}+V^{eq}(x)\right), \quad P^{eq}(x)=g\left(\alpha_{P}-V^{eq}(x)\right), \quad x \in \Omega, \end{equation} while $V^{eq}$ satisfies the following elliptic problem \begin{equation} \left\{\begin{array}{ll} \Delta V^{eq}=g\left(\alpha_{N}+V^{eq}\right)-g\left(\alpha_{P}-V^{eq}\right)-C \text{ in } \Omega, &\\ V^{eq}(x)=\overline{V}(x) \text{ on } \Gamma^{D}, \quad \nabla V^{eq}\cdot \mathbf{n}=0 \text{ on } \Gamma^{N}.&\end{array}\right. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Thermal equilibrium densities as g of alpha plus/minus V^eq, with V^eq solving a nonlinear Poisson problem.

nodes.name: Thermal equilibrium densities
nodes.statement: N^{eq}(x)=g\left(\alpha_{N}+V^{eq}(x)\right), \quad P^{eq}(x)=g\left(\alpha_{P}-V^{eq}(x)\right), \quad x \in \Omega,
nodes.label: eqNP

nodes.name: Elliptic problem for V^eq
nodes.statement: \left\{\begin{array}{ll} \Delta V^{eq}=g\left(\alpha_{N}+V^{eq}\right)-g\left(\alpha_{P}-V^{eq}\right)-C \text{ in } \Omega, &\\ V^{eq}(x)=\overline{V}(x) \text{ on } \Gamma^{D}, \quad \nabla V^{eq}\cdot \mathbf{n}=0 \text{ on } \Gamma^{N}.&\end{array}\right.
nodes.label: eqV

nodes.name: Leibenzon-Muskat model
nodes.statement: The flow of a gas in a $d$-dimensional porous medium is classically described by the Leibenzon-Muskat model, \begin{equation} \left\{\begin{array}{lcl} \partial_{t}v=\Delta v^{\gamma} & & \text{ on } \mathbb{R}^{d}\times(0,T),\\ v(x,0)=v_{0}(x) & & \text{ on } \mathbb{R}^{d},\end{array}\right. \end{equation} where the function $v$ represents the density of the gas in the porous medium and $\gamma>1$ is a physical constant.

nodes.name: Porous media equation
nodes.statement: \left\{\begin{array}{lcl} \partial_{t}v=\Delta v^{\gamma} & & \text{ on } \mathbb{R}^{d}\times(0,T),\\ v(x,0)=v_{0}(x) & & \text{ on } \mathbb{R}^{d},\end{array}\right.
nodes.label: pm

nodes.name: Nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation
nodes.statement: With a time-dependent scaling (see \cite{Carrillo2000}), we transform (\ref{pm}) into the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation \begin{equation} \left\{\begin{array}{lcl} \partial_{t}u=\text{div}(xu+\nabla u^{\gamma}) & & \text{ on } \mathbb{R}^{d}\times(0,T),\\ u(x,0)=u_{0}(x)& & \text{ on } \mathbb{R}^{d}.\end{array}\right. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Rescaled porous media equation (nonlinear Fokker-Planck)
nodes.statement: \left\{\begin{array}{lcl} \partial_{t}u=\text{div}(xu+\nabla u^{\gamma}) & & \text{ on } \mathbb{R}^{d}\times(0,T),\\ u(x,0)=u_{0}(x)& & \text{ on } \mathbb{R}^{d}.\end{array}\right.
nodes.label: PM

nodes.name: Barenblatt-Pattle stationary solution
nodes.statement: It is proved in \cite{Carrillo2000} that the unique stationary solution of (\ref{PM}) is given by the Barenblatt-Pattle type formula \begin{equation} u^{eq}(x)=\left(C_{1}-\frac{\gamma -1}{2\gamma}|x|^{2}\right)_{+}^{1/(\gamma -1)}, \end{equation} where $C_{1}$ is a constant such that $u^{eq}$ has the same mass as the initial data $u_{0}$.
assumptions: $C_{1}$ is a constant such that $u^{eq}$ has the same mass as the initial data $u_{0}$
conclusions: the unique stationary solution of (\ref{PM}) is given by the Barenblatt-Pattle type formula
also_stated_at: We recall that the unique stationary solution $u^{eq}$ of the porous media equation (\ref{PM}) is given by the Barenblatt-Pattle type formula (\ref{barenblatt}), where $C_{1}$ is such that $u^{eq}$ as the same mass as the initial data $u_{0}$.

nodes.name: Barenblatt-Pattle formula
nodes.statement: u^{eq}(x)=\left(C_{1}-\frac{\gamma -1}{2\gamma}|x|^{2}\right)_{+}^{1/(\gamma -1)},
nodes.label: barenblatt

nodes.name: Convergence to the Barenblatt-Pattle solution (Carrillo-Toscani)
nodes.statement: Moreover, J. A. Carrillo and G. Toscani have proved in \cite{Carrillo2000} the convergence of the solution $u(x,t)$ of (\ref{pm}) to the Barenblatt-Pattle solution $u^{eq}(x)$ as $t \rightarrow \infty$.
conclusions: the convergence of the solution $u(x,t)$ of (\ref{pm}) to the Barenblatt-Pattle solution $u^{eq}(x)$ as $t \rightarrow \infty$

nodes.name: Relative entropy and entropy dissipation (porous media)
nodes.statement: As in the case of the drift-diffusion model, the proof of the convergence to the Barenblatt-Pattle solution is based on an entropy estimate with the control of the entropy dissipation given by (\ref{inegentropie}), where the relative entropy is defined by \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}(t)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\left(H(u(t))-H(u^{eq})+\frac{|x|^{2}}{2}\left(u(t)-u^{eq}\right)\right)dx, \end{equation} where $H$ is defined by (\ref{H}) and the entropy dissipation is given by \begin{equation} \mathcal{I}(t)=-\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal{E}(t)=-\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}u(t)\left\vert \nabla\left(h(u(t))+\frac{|x|^{2}}{2}\right) \right\vert^{2}dx. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Relative entropy w.r.t. the Barenblatt-Pattle profile and its dissipation, controlled as in the energy estimate.

nodes.name: Relative entropy (porous media)
nodes.statement: \mathcal{E}(t)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\left(H(u(t))-H(u^{eq})+\frac{|x|^{2}}{2}\left(u(t)-u^{eq}\right)\right)dx,
nodes.label: Econtinupm

nodes.name: Entropy dissipation (porous media)
nodes.statement: \mathcal{I}(t)=-\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal{E}(t)=-\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}u(t)\left\vert \nabla\left(h(u(t))+\frac{|x|^{2}}{2}\right) \right\vert^{2}dx.
nodes.label: Icontinupm

nodes.name: Importance of equilibrium-preserving fluxes
nodes.statement: Looking at these results, it seems crucial that the numerical flux preserves the thermal equilibrium to obtain the consistency of the approximate solution in the long time asymptotic limit.

nodes.name: Convection-diffusion problem with nonlinear diffusion
nodes.statement: We will now consider the following problem: \begin{equation} \partial_{t}u-\text{div}(\nabla r(u)-\mathbf{q}u)=0 \text{ for } (x,t) \in \Omega \times (0,T), \end{equation} with an initial condition \begin{equation} u(x,0)=u_{0}(x) \text{ for } x \in \Omega. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Nonlinear convection-diffusion equation
nodes.statement: \partial_{t}u-\text{div}(\nabla r(u)-\mathbf{q}u)=0 \text{ for } (x,t) \in \Omega \times (0,T),
nodes.label: eq

nodes.name: Initial condition
nodes.statement: u(x,0)=u_{0}(x) \text{ for } x \in \Omega.
nodes.label: CI

nodes.name: Dirichlet-Neumann boundary conditions
nodes.statement: The boundary $\partial \Omega=\Gamma$ is split into two parts $\Gamma=\Gamma^{D} \cup \Gamma^{N}$ and, if we denote by $\mathbf{n}$ the outward normal to $\Gamma$, the boundary conditions are Dirichlet boundary conditions on $\Gamma^{D}$ \begin{equation} u(x,t)=\overline{u}(x,t) \text{ for } (x,t) \in \Gamma^{D} \times (0,T), \end{equation} and homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions on $\Gamma^{N}$: \begin{equation} \nabla r(u) \cdot \mathbf{n}=0 \text{ on } \Gamma^{N} \times (0,T). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Dirichlet boundary condition
nodes.statement: u(x,t)=\overline{u}(x,t) \text{ for } (x,t) \in \Gamma^{D} \times (0,T),
nodes.label: BCD

nodes.name: Homogeneous Neumann boundary condition
nodes.statement: \nabla r(u) \cdot \mathbf{n}=0 \text{ on } \Gamma^{N} \times (0,T).
nodes.label: BCN

nodes.name: Dirichlet boundary conditions for the analysis
nodes.statement: We will construct the scheme and perform some numerical experiments in the case of Dirichlet-Neumann boundary conditions. However, for the analysis of the scheme, we will only consider the case of Dirichlet boundary conditions ($\partial\Omega=\Gamma^{D}=\Gamma$).

nodes.name: Hypotheses (H1)-(H5)
nodes.statement: We suppose that the following hypotheses are fulfilled: \begin{description} \item[(H1)] $\Omega$ is an open bounded connected subset of $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, with $d=1,2$ or $3$, \item[(H2)] $\partial\Omega=\Gamma^{D}=\Gamma$, $\overline{u}$ is the trace on $\Gamma \times (0,T)$ of a function, also denoted $\overline{u}$, which is assumed to satisfy $\overline{u} \in H^{1}(\Omega \times (0,T))\cap L^{\infty}(\Omega \times (0,T))$ and $\overline{u} \geq 0\textit{ a.e.}$, \item[(H3)] $u_{0} \in L^{\infty}(\Omega)$ and $u_{0} \geq 0 \textit{ a.e.}$, \item[(H4)] $r \in C^{2}(\mathbb{R})$ is strictly increasing on $]0,+\infty[$, $r(0)=r'(0)=0$, with $r'(s)\geq c_{0}s^{\gamma-1}$, \item[(H5)] $\mathbf{q} \in C^{1}(\overline{\Omega},\mathbb{R}^{d})$. \end{description}
nodes.statement_short: Bounded domain in d<=3, nonnegative bounded data, r C^2 increasing with r'(s)>=c0 s^(gamma-1), q of class C^1.

nodes.name: Distance d_sigma
nodes.statement: We note for all $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}$ \begin{equation*} d_{\sigma}=\left\{\begin{array}{lll} \text{d}(x_{K},x_{L}), & \text{ for } \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int},& \sigma=K|L,\\ \text{d}(x_{K},\sigma), & \text{ for } \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}.\end{array}\right. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 2.1 Definition of the finite volume scheme

nodes.name: Transmissibility coefficient
nodes.statement: For all $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}$, we define the transmissibility coefficient $\displaystyle{\tau_{\sigma}=\frac{\text{m}(\sigma)}{d_{\sigma}}.}$
nodes.section: 2.1 Definition of the finite volume scheme

nodes.name: Outward unit normal n_{K,sigma}
nodes.statement: For $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}$, $\mathbf{n}_{K,\sigma}$ is the unit vector normal to $\sigma$ outward to $K$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Definition of the finite volume scheme

nodes.name: Space-time discretization
nodes.statement: Let $(\mathcal{T},\mathcal{E},(x_{K})_{K \in \mathcal{T}})$ be an admissible discretization of $\Omega$ and let us define the time step $\Delta t$, $N_{T}=E(T/\Delta t)$ and the increasing sequence $(t^{n})_{0\leq n \leq N_{T}}$, where $t^{n}=n\Delta t$, in order to get a space-time discretization $\mathcal{D}$ of $\Omega \times (0,T)$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Definition of the finite volume scheme

nodes.name: Size of the space-time discretization
nodes.statement: The size of the space-time discretization $\mathcal{D}$ is defined by: \begin{equation*} \delta =\max(\Delta x, \Delta t). \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 2.1 Definition of the finite volume scheme

nodes.name: Discretized initial condition
nodes.statement: First of all, the initial condition is discretized by: \begin{equation} U^{0}_{K}=\frac{1}{\text{m}(K)}\int_{K}u_{0}(x)\,dx, \quad K \in \mathcal{T}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 2.1 Definition of the finite volume scheme

nodes.name: Discrete initial condition
nodes.statement: U^{0}_{K}=\frac{1}{\text{m}(K)}\int_{K}u_{0}(x)\,dx, \quad K \in \mathcal{T}.
nodes.section: 2.1 Definition of the finite volume scheme
nodes.label: CId

nodes.name: Numerical boundary conditions
nodes.statement: In order to introduce the finite volume scheme, we also need to define the numerical boundary conditions: \begin{equation} U^{n+1}_{\sigma}=\frac{1}{\Delta t \, \text{m}(\sigma)}\int_{t^{n}}^{t^{n+1}}\int_{\sigma}\overline{u}(s,t)\,ds \, dt, \quad \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext}^{D}, \,\ n\geq 0. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 2.1 Definition of the finite volume scheme

nodes.name: Discrete Dirichlet boundary values
nodes.statement: U^{n+1}_{\sigma}=\frac{1}{\Delta t \, \text{m}(\sigma)}\int_{t^{n}}^{t^{n+1}}\int_{\sigma}\overline{u}(s,t)\,ds \, dt, \quad \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext}^{D}, \,\ n\geq 0.
nodes.section: 2.1 Definition of the finite volume scheme
nodes.label: BCd

nodes.name: Discrete normal velocity q_{K,sigma}
nodes.statement: We set \begin{equation} q_{K,\sigma}=\frac{1}{\text{m}(\sigma)}\int_{\sigma}\mathbf{q}(x)\cdot \mathbf{n}_{K,\sigma}\,ds(x), \quad \forall K \in \mathcal{T}, \quad \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 2.1 Definition of the finite volume scheme

nodes.name: Mean normal velocity on an edge
nodes.statement: q_{K,\sigma}=\frac{1}{\text{m}(\sigma)}\int_{\sigma}\mathbf{q}(x)\cdot \mathbf{n}_{K,\sigma}\,ds(x), \quad \forall K \in \mathcal{T}, \quad \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}.
nodes.section: 2.1 Definition of the finite volume scheme
nodes.label: q

nodes.name: Finite volume scheme (backward Euler)
nodes.statement: Then the scheme on $u$ is given by the following set of equations: \begin{equation} \text{m}(K)\frac{U_{K}^{n+1}-U_{K}^{n}}{\Delta t}+\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}} \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}=0, \end{equation} where the numerical flux $\mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}$ is an approximation of $\displaystyle{-\int_{\sigma} (\nabla r(u)-\mathbf{q}u)\cdot \mathbf{n}_{K,\sigma}}$ which remains to be defined.
nodes.section: 2.1 Definition of the finite volume scheme
nodes.statement_short: Backward Euler finite volume scheme: mass balance on each control volume with numerical fluxes through its edges.

nodes.name: Finite volume scheme
nodes.statement: \text{m}(K)\frac{U_{K}^{n+1}-U_{K}^{n}}{\Delta t}+\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}} \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}=0,
nodes.section: 2.1 Definition of the finite volume scheme
nodes.label: schemegene

nodes.name: Classical upwind flux
nodes.statement: The definition of this flux is \begin{equation} \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}= \left\{\begin{array}{lll} \tau_{\sigma} \left(r\left(U_{K}^{n+1}\right)-r\left(U_{L}^{n+1}\right)+d_{\sigma}\left(q_{K,\sigma}^{+}U_{K}^{n+1}-q_{K,\sigma}^{-}U_{L}^{n+1}\right)\right), & & \forall \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K},\\ \tau_{\sigma} \left(r\left(U_{K}^{n+1}\right)-r\left(U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right)+d_{\sigma}\left(q_{K,\sigma}^{+}U_{K}^{n+1}-q_{K,\sigma}^{-}U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right)\right),& & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D},\\ 0, & & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{N}, \end{array}\right. \end{equation} where $s^{+}=\max(s,0)$ and $s^{-}=\max(-s,0)$ are the positive and negative parts of a real number $s$.
nodes.statement_short: Two-point flux for the diffusion term and upwinding of the convection term.

nodes.name: Classical upwind flux
nodes.statement: \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}= \left\{\begin{array}{lll} \tau_{\sigma} \left(r\left(U_{K}^{n+1}\right)-r\left(U_{L}^{n+1}\right)+d_{\sigma}\left(q_{K,\sigma}^{+}U_{K}^{n+1}-q_{K,\sigma}^{-}U_{L}^{n+1}\right)\right), & & \forall \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K},\\ \tau_{\sigma} \left(r\left(U_{K}^{n+1}\right)-r\left(U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right)+d_{\sigma}\left(q_{K,\sigma}^{+}U_{K}^{n+1}-q_{K,\sigma}^{-}U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right)\right),& & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D},\\ 0, & & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{N}, \end{array}\right.
nodes.label: upwindclass

nodes.name: Upwind flux with nonlinear discretization of the diffusion term
nodes.statement: The flux is then defined with a standard upwinding for the convective term and a nonlinear approximation for the diffusive term: \begin{eqnarray*} & &\mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}= \\ & &\left\{\begin{array}{lll}-\tau_{\sigma}\left(\min\left(U_{K}^{n+1},U_{L}^{n+1}\right)Dh\left(U^{n+1}\right)_{K,\sigma}+d_{\sigma}\left(q_{K,\sigma}^{+}U_{K}^{n+1}-q_{K,\sigma}^{-}U_{L}^{n+1}\right)\right), & & \forall \sigma=K|L,\\ -\tau_{\sigma}\left(\min\left(U_{K}^{n+1},U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right)Dh\left(U^{n+1}\right)_{K,\sigma}+d_{\sigma}\left(q_{K,\sigma}^{+}U_{K}^{n+1}-q_{K,\sigma}^{-}U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right)\right), & & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}, \\ 0, & & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{N}, \end{array}\right. \end{eqnarray*} where for a given function $f$, $Df(U)_{K,\sigma}$ is defined by \begin{equation*} Df(U)_{K,\sigma}=\left\{\begin{array}{lll} f(U_{L})-f(U_{K}), & & \text{ if } \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{K,int}, \\ f(U_{\sigma})-f(U_{K}), & & \text{ if } \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K,ext}^{D}, \\ 0, & & \text{ if } \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K,ext}^{N}.\end{array}\right. \end{equation*}
definiendum: upwind flux with nonlinear discretization of the diffusion term
nodes.statement_short: Upwinded convection plus a min(U_K,U_L) times discrete enthalpy difference for diffusion.

nodes.name: Equilibrium preservation and long-time convergence of the nonlinear upwind scheme
nodes.statement: This flux preserves the thermal equilibrium and it is proved that the numerical solution converges to this equilibrium when time goes to infinity.
conclusions: This flux preserves the thermal equilibrium
the numerical solution converges to this equilibrium when time goes to infinity

nodes.name: Properties of the Scharfetter-Gummel flux
nodes.statement: The Scharfetter-Gummel flux preserves steady-state, and is second order accurate in space (see \cite{Lazarov1996}).
conclusions: The Scharfetter-Gummel flux preserves steady-state
is second order accurate in space

nodes.name: Scharfetter-Gummel flux
nodes.statement: It is defined by: \begin{equation*} \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}=\left\{\begin{array}{lll}\tau_{\sigma}\left(B(-d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma})U_{K}^{n+1}-B(d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma})U_{L}^{n+1}\right), & & \forall \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{K,int},\\ \tau_{\sigma}\left(B(-d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma})U_{K}^{n+1}-B(d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma})U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right), & & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K,ext}^{D},\\ 0, & & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K,ext}^{N},\end{array}\right. \end{equation*} where $B$ is the Bernoulli function defined by \begin{equation*} B(x)=\frac{x}{e^{x}-1} \text{ for } x \neq 0, \quad B(0)=1. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Exponentially fitted two-point flux for linear diffusion weighted by the Bernoulli function B(x)=x/(e^x-1).

nodes.name: Scharfetter-Gummel flux with viscosity
nodes.statement: Firstly, if we consider the linear case with a viscosity coefficient $\varepsilon>0$, namely \begin{equation*} \partial_{t}u-\text{div}(\varepsilon \nabla u-\mathbf{q}u)=0 \text{ for } (x,t) \in \Omega \times (0,T), \end{equation*} then the Scharfetter-Gummel flux is defined by: \begin{equation} \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}= \tau_{\sigma} \varepsilon \left(B\left(\frac{-d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{\varepsilon}\right)U_{K}^{n+1}-B\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{\varepsilon}\right)U_{L}^{n+1}\right) \quad \forall \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Scharfetter-Gummel flux with viscosity
nodes.statement: \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}= \tau_{\sigma} \varepsilon \left(B\left(\frac{-d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{\varepsilon}\right)U_{K}^{n+1}-B\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{\varepsilon}\right)U_{L}^{n+1}\right) \quad \forall \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}.
nodes.label: sgvisc

nodes.name: Vanishing-viscosity limit of the Scharfetter-Gummel flux is upwind
nodes.statement: Using the following properties of the Bernoulli function: \begin{equation*} B(s) \underset{s \rightarrow +\infty}{\longrightarrow} 0 \text{ and } B(s) \underset{-\infty}{\sim} -s, \end{equation*} it is clear that if $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, this flux degenerates into the classical upwind flux for the transport equation $\partial_{t}u-\text{div}(\textbf{q}u)=0$: \begin{equation} \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}= \text{m}(\sigma)\left(q_{K,\sigma}^{+}U_{K}^{n+1}-q_{K,\sigma}^{-}U_{L}^{n+1}\right) \quad \forall \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}. \end{equation}
conclusions: this flux degenerates into the classical upwind flux for the transport equation $\partial_{t}u-\text{div}(\textbf{q}u)=0$

nodes.name: Upwind flux for the transport equation
nodes.statement: \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}= \text{m}(\sigma)\left(q_{K,\sigma}^{+}U_{K}^{n+1}-q_{K,\sigma}^{-}U_{L}^{n+1}\right) \quad \forall \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}.
nodes.label: upwindtransport

nodes.name: Interface approximation dr_{K,sigma}
nodes.statement: We denote by $dr_{K,\sigma}$ an approximation of $r'(u)$ at the interface $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}$, which will be defined later.

nodes.name: Extension of the Scharfetter-Gummel flux to nonlinear diffusion
nodes.statement: We consider this term as a viscosity coefficient and then, using (\ref{sgvisc}), we extend the Scharfetter-Gummel flux by defining: \begin{equation} \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}=\left\{\begin{array}{lll} \displaystyle{\tau_{\sigma} dr_{K,\sigma} \left(B\left(\frac{-d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}\right)U_{K}^{n+1}-B\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}\right)U_{L}^{n+1}\right),}& & \forall \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}, \\ \displaystyle{\tau_{\sigma} dr_{K,\sigma} \left(B\left(\frac{-d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}\right)U_{K}^{n+1}-B\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}\right)U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right),}& & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}, \\ 0, & & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{N}. \end{array}\right. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Scharfetter-Gummel flux with the viscosity replaced by an interface approximation dr of r'(u).

nodes.name: Extended Scharfetter-Gummel flux
nodes.statement: \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}=\left\{\begin{array}{lll} \displaystyle{\tau_{\sigma} dr_{K,\sigma} \left(B\left(\frac{-d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}\right)U_{K}^{n+1}-B\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}\right)U_{L}^{n+1}\right),}& & \forall \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}, \\ \displaystyle{\tau_{\sigma} dr_{K,\sigma} \left(B\left(\frac{-d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}\right)U_{K}^{n+1}-B\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}\right)U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right),}& & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}, \\ 0, & & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{N}. \end{array}\right.
nodes.label: sgext

nodes.name: Degenerate case reduces to upwind
nodes.statement: In the degenerate case, $dr_{K,\sigma}$ can vanish and then this flux degenerates into the upwind flux (\ref{upwindtransport}).
assumptions: In the degenerate case, $dr_{K,\sigma}$ can vanish
conclusions: this flux degenerates into the upwind flux (\ref{upwindtransport})

nodes.name: First choice of dr (arithmetic mean)
nodes.statement: A first possibility is to take the value of $r'$ at the average of $U_{K}$ and $U_{\sigma}$: \begin{equation} dr_{K,\sigma}=\left\{\begin{array}{lll} \displaystyle{r'\left(\frac{U_{K}+U_{L}}{2}\right),} & & \forall \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}, \\ \displaystyle{r'\left(\frac{U_{K}+U_{\sigma}}{2}\right),} & & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}. \end{array}\right. \end{equation}

nodes.name: dr at the arithmetic mean
nodes.statement: dr_{K,\sigma}=\left\{\begin{array}{lll} \displaystyle{r'\left(\frac{U_{K}+U_{L}}{2}\right),} & & \forall \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}, \\ \displaystyle{r'\left(\frac{U_{K}+U_{\sigma}}{2}\right),} & & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}. \end{array}\right.
nodes.label: dr1

nodes.name: Closeness to the Juengel-Pietra choice
nodes.statement: This choice is quite close to the one of A. Jüngel and P. Pietra (see \cite{Juengel1995,Juengel1997}).

nodes.name: Function dr (equilibrium-preserving)
nodes.statement: Therefore, we define the function $dr$ as follows: for $a$, $b \in \mathbb{R}_{+}$, \begin{equation} dr(a,b)=\left\{ \begin{array}{rll} \displaystyle{\frac{h(b)-h(a)}{\log(b)-\log(a)}} & &\text{ if } ab>0 \text{ and } a \neq b,\\ \displaystyle{r'\left(\frac{a+b}{2}\right)} & &\text{ elsewhere, } \end{array} \right. \end{equation} and we set for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$ \begin{equation} dr_{K,\sigma}=\left\{\begin{array}{lll} dr(U_{K},U_{L}), & & \text{ for } \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{K,int}, \\ dr(U_{K},U_{\sigma}), & & \text{ for } \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K,ext}^{D}.\end{array}\right. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: dr(a,b) = (h(b)-h(a))/(log b - log a) for distinct positive a,b, else r' at the mean; dr_{K,sigma}=dr(U_K,U_L).

nodes.name: Definition of dr(a,b)
nodes.statement: dr(a,b)=\left\{ \begin{array}{rll} \displaystyle{\frac{h(b)-h(a)}{\log(b)-\log(a)}} & &\text{ if } ab>0 \text{ and } a \neq b,\\ \displaystyle{r'\left(\frac{a+b}{2}\right)} & &\text{ elsewhere, } \end{array} \right.
nodes.label: defdr

nodes.name: dr_{K,sigma} from dr
nodes.statement: dr_{K,\sigma}=\left\{\begin{array}{lll} dr(U_{K},U_{L}), & & \text{ for } \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{K,int}, \\ dr(U_{K},U_{\sigma}), & & \text{ for } \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K,ext}^{D}.\end{array}\right.
nodes.label: dr2

nodes.name: Steady-state preservation remark
nodes.statement: Let $K \in \mathcal{T}$ and $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}$. We assume that $dr_{K,\sigma}$ is defined by (\ref{dr2}) in (\ref{sgext}) and that $U_{K}>0$ and $U_{\sigma}>0$. If $d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}=Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}$, then $\mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}=0$.\\ Indeed, \begin{eqnarray*} \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma} & = & \tau_{\sigma}dr_{K,\sigma}\left(B\left(-\frac{Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}\right)U_{K}-B\left(\frac{Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}\right)U_{\sigma}\right)\\ &=& \tau_{\sigma}Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}\left(\frac{\exp\left(\displaystyle{\frac{Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}}\right)U_{K}-U_{\sigma}}{\exp\left(\displaystyle{\frac{Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}}\right)-1}\right). \end{eqnarray*} But using the definition (\ref{defdr}) of $dr$, we obtain \begin{equation*} \exp\left(\displaystyle{\frac{Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}}\right)=\frac{U_{\sigma}}{U_{K}}, \end{equation*} and then $ \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}=0$. Thus the scheme preserves this type of steady-state.
nodes.statement_short: When d_sigma q_{K,sigma} equals the discrete enthalpy jump, the extended flux vanishes, so such steady states are preserved.

nodes.name: Extended flux vanishes at discrete thermal equilibrium
nodes.statement: Let $K \in \mathcal{T}$ and $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}$. We assume that $dr_{K,\sigma}$ is defined by (\ref{dr2}) in (\ref{sgext}) and that $U_{K}>0$ and $U_{\sigma}>0$. If $d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}=Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}$, then $\mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}=0$.
conclusions: $\mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}=0$

nodes.name: Proof that the extended flux vanishes at equilibrium
nodes.statement: Indeed, \begin{eqnarray*} \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma} & = & \tau_{\sigma}dr_{K,\sigma}\left(B\left(-\frac{Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}\right)U_{K}-B\left(\frac{Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}\right)U_{\sigma}\right)\\ &=& \tau_{\sigma}Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}\left(\frac{\exp\left(\displaystyle{\frac{Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}}\right)U_{K}-U_{\sigma}}{\exp\left(\displaystyle{\frac{Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}}\right)-1}\right). \end{eqnarray*} But using the definition (\ref{defdr}) of $dr$, we obtain \begin{equation*} \exp\left(\displaystyle{\frac{Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}}\right)=\frac{U_{\sigma}}{U_{K}}, \end{equation*} and then $ \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}=0$. Thus the scheme preserves this type of steady-state.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute d q = Dh into the flux and use the definition of dr to get exp(Dh/dr)=U_sigma/U_K, so the numerator vanishes.

nodes.name: Explicit time discretization of dr
nodes.statement: We choose an explicit expression of $dr_{K,\sigma}$: \begin{equation} dr_{K,\sigma}^{n}=\left\{\begin{array}{lll} dr(U_{K}^{n},U_{L}^{n}), & & \text{ for } \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{K,int}, \\ dr(U_{K}^{n},U_{\sigma}^{n}), & & \text{ for } \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K,ext}^{D}.\end{array}\right. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Explicit dr^n
nodes.statement: dr_{K,\sigma}^{n}=\left\{\begin{array}{lll} dr(U_{K}^{n},U_{L}^{n}), & & \text{ for } \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{K,int}, \\ dr(U_{K}^{n},U_{\sigma}^{n}), & & \text{ for } \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K,ext}^{D}.\end{array}\right.
nodes.label: dr3

nodes.name: Linear system at each time step
nodes.statement: Thus we obtain a scheme which leads only to solve a linear system of equations at each time step.

nodes.name: Scharfetter-Gummel extended flux
nodes.statement: To sum up, our extension of the Scharfetter-Gummel flux is defined by \begin{equation} \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}=\left\{\begin{array}{lcl} \tau_{\sigma} dr_{K,\sigma}^{n} \left(B\left(\displaystyle{\frac{-d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}^{n}}}\right)U_{K}^{n+1}-B\left(\displaystyle{\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}^{n}}}\right)U_{L}^{n+1}\right), & & \forall \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{K,int}, \\ \tau_{\sigma} dr_{K,\sigma}^{n} \left(B\left(\displaystyle{\frac{-d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}^{n}}}\right)U_{K}^{n+1}-B\left(\displaystyle{\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}^{n}}}\right)U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right), & & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K,ext}^{D}, \\ 0, & & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K,ext}^{N},\end{array}\right. \end{equation} where $dr_{K,\sigma}^{n}$ is defined by (\ref{dr3}).
nodes.statement_short: The proposed SG-ext flux: Scharfetter-Gummel flux with explicit equilibrium-preserving interface diffusion dr^n.

nodes.name: Scharfetter-Gummel extended flux
nodes.statement: \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}=\left\{\begin{array}{lcl} \tau_{\sigma} dr_{K,\sigma}^{n} \left(B\left(\displaystyle{\frac{-d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}^{n}}}\right)U_{K}^{n+1}-B\left(\displaystyle{\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}^{n}}}\right)U_{L}^{n+1}\right), & & \forall \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{K,int}, \\ \tau_{\sigma} dr_{K,\sigma}^{n} \left(B\left(\displaystyle{\frac{-d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}^{n}}}\right)U_{K}^{n+1}-B\left(\displaystyle{\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}^{n}}}\right)U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right), & & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K,ext}^{D}, \\ 0, & & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K,ext}^{N},\end{array}\right.
nodes.label: flux

nodes.name: The extended flux preserves the equilibrium
nodes.statement: This flux preserves the equilibrium.
conclusions: This flux preserves the equilibrium.

nodes.name: Mean-value property of dr
nodes.statement: Let $a$, $b \in \mathbb{R}$, $a,b \geq 0$. Then there exists $\eta \in [\min(a,b),\max(a,b)]$ such that \begin{equation*} dr(a,b)=r'(\eta). \end{equation*}
conclusions: there exists $\eta \in [\min(a,b),\max(a,b)]$ such that \begin{equation*} dr(a,b)=r'(\eta). \end{equation*}
nodes.label: propdr

nodes.name: Proof of the mean-value property of dr
nodes.statement: The result is clear if $ab=0$ or $a=b$. Let us suppose that $ab>0$ and $a < b$ (the proof is the same if $a>b$). If we consider the change of variables $x=\log(a)$ and $y=\log(b)$, we obtain \begin{equation*} dr(a,b)=\frac{h(\exp(y))-h(\exp(x))}{y-x} \end{equation*} and using Taylor's formula, there exists $\theta \in [x,y]$ such that \begin{equation*} dr(a,b)=\exp(\theta)h'(\exp(\theta))=r'(\exp(\theta)) \text{ (using the definition of $h$). } \end{equation*} Finally, there exists $\eta=\exp(\theta) \in [a,b]$ such that \begin{equation*} dr(a,b)=r'(\eta). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Change variables to logarithms and apply the mean value theorem (Taylor) to h(exp(.)), using h'=r'/s.

nodes.name: Centred form of the extended flux
nodes.statement: The flux (\ref{flux}) can also be written as \begin{equation} \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}=\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}\frac{U_{K}^{n+1}+U^{n+1}_{\sigma}}{2}-\frac{\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}}{2}\coth \left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right)(U^{n+1}_{\sigma}-U^{n+1}_{K}). \end{equation} The first term is a centred discretization of the convective part. The second term is consistent with the diffusive part of equation (\ref{eq}), since $\displaystyle{\coth(x)\underset{0}{\sim}\frac{1}{x}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Extended flux = centred convection term minus coth-weighted diffusion term, consistent with the diffusion since coth x ~ 1/x.

nodes.name: Coth form of the flux
nodes.statement: \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}=\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}\frac{U_{K}^{n+1}+U^{n+1}_{\sigma}}{2}-\frac{\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}}{2}\coth \left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right)(U^{n+1}_{\sigma}-U^{n+1}_{K}).
nodes.label: flux2

nodes.name: Existence, uniqueness and L-infinity estimate for the scheme
nodes.statement: Let us assume hypotheses (H1)-(H5). Let $\mathcal{D}$ be an admissible discretization of $\Omega \times (0,T)$. Then there exists a unique solution $\lbrace U_{K}^{n},K \in \mathcal{T},0\leq n \leq N_{T}\rbrace$ to the scheme (\ref{CId})-(\ref{BCd})-(\ref{schemegene})-(\ref{flux}), with $U_{K}^{n} \geq 0$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$ and $0\leq n \leq N_{T}$.\\ Moreover, if we suppose that the two following assumptions are fulfilled: \begin{description} \item[(H6)] $ \emph{div} (\mathbf{q})=0$, \item[(H7)] there exist two constants $m>0$ and $M>0$ such that $m\leq \overline{u},u_{0}\leq M$, \end{description} then we have \begin{equation} 0 <m \leq U^{n}_{K} \leq M, \quad \forall K \in \mathcal{T}, \quad \forall n \geq 0. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proof of well-posedness and L-infinity estimate
nodes.statement: At each time step, the scheme (\ref{CId})-(\ref{BCd})-(\ref{schemegene})-(\ref{flux}) leads to a system of card$(\mathcal{T})$ linear equations on $U^{n+1}=(U^{n+1}_{K})_{K \in \mathcal{T}}$ which can be written: \begin{equation*} A^{n}U^{n+1}=S^{n}, \end{equation*} where : \begin{itemize} \item[$\bullet$] $A^{n}$ is the matrix defined by \begin{alignat*}{3} &A^{n}_{K,K} & = & \frac{\text{m}(K)}{\Delta t}+\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}}\tau_{\sigma}dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}B\left(\frac{-d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right) \,\ \forall K \in \mathcal{T},\\ &A^{n}_{K,L} & = & -\tau_{\sigma}dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}B\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right) \,\ \forall L \in \mathcal{T} \text{ such that } \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}; \end{alignat*} \item[$\bullet$] $\displaystyle{S^{n}=\left(\frac{\text{m}(K)}{\Delta t}U^{n}_{K}\right)_{K \in \mathcal{T}}+Tb^{n}}$, with \begin{equation*} Tb^{n}_{K} = \left\{\begin{array}{ll} 0 & \text{ if } K \in \mathcal{T} \text{ such that } \text{m}(\partial K\cap \Gamma)=0,\\ \displaystyle{\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}}\tau_{\sigma}dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}B\left(\displaystyle{\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}}\right)U^{n+1}_{\sigma}} & \text{ if } K \in \mathcal{T} \text{ such that } \text{m}(\partial K\cap \Gamma)\neq 0. \end{array}\right. \end{equation*} \end{itemize} The diagonal terms of $A^{n}$ are positive and the offdiagonal terms are nonnegative (since $B(x)>0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and $dr^{n}_{K,\sigma} \geq 0$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$, for all $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}$). Moreover, since $dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}=dr_{L,\sigma}^{n}$ and $q_{K,\sigma}=-q_{L,\sigma}$ for all $ \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int}$, we have for all $L \in \mathcal{T}$: \begin{equation*} \left|A^{n}_{L,L}\right|-\sum_{\substack{K \in \mathcal{T} \\ K \neq L}}\left|A^{n}_{K,L}\right|=\frac{\text{m}(L)}{\Delta t}>0, \end{equation*} and then $A^{n}$ is strictly diagonally dominant with respect to the columns. $A^{n}$ is then an M-matrix so $A^{n}$ is invertible, which gives existence and uniqueness of the solution of the scheme. Moreover, $(A^{n})^{-1}\geq 0$ and since $U_{K}^{0} \geq 0$ for all $K\in \mathcal{T}$ (using (H3)) and $U^{n+1}_{\sigma} \geq 0$ for all $n \geq 0$, for all $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext}^{D}$ (using (H2)), it is easy to prove by induction that $U^{n}_{K} \geq 0$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$, for all $n \geq 0$.\\ Now, we suppose that (H6) and (H7) are fulfilled. We prove that $U^{n}_{K}\leq M $ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$, for all $n \geq 0$ by induction. Thanks to hypothesis (H7), we have clearly $U^{0}_{K}\leq M $ for all $ K \in \mathcal{T}$.\\ Let us suppose that $U^{n}_{K}\leq M \quad \forall K \in \mathcal{T}$. We want to prove $U^{n+1}_{K}\leq M \quad \forall K \in \mathcal{T}$.\\ Let us define $\textbf{M}=(M,...,M)^{T} \in \mathbb{R}^{\text{card}(\mathcal{T})}$. Since $A^{n}$ is an M-matrix, we have $(A^{n})^{-1} \geq 0$ and then it suffices to prove that $A^{n}\left(U^{n+1}-\textbf{M}\right) \leq 0$. \\ We first compute $A^{n}\textbf{M}$. Using the following property of the Bernoulli function: \begin{equation} B(x)-B(-x)=-x \quad \forall x \in \mathbb{R}, \end{equation} we obtain that for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$, \begin{equation*} \left(A^{n}\textbf{M}\right)_{K}=M\left(\frac{\text{m}(K)}{\Delta t}+\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}}\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}+\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}}\tau_{\sigma}dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}B\left(-\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right)\right). \end{equation*} Then we compute $A^{n}\left(U^{n+1}-\textbf{M}\right)$: for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$ \begin{eqnarray*} \left(A^{n}\left(U^{n+1}-\textbf{M}\right)\right)_{K} &=& \frac{\text{m}(K)}{\Delta t}(U^{n}_{K}-M)+ \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}}\tau_{\sigma}dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}B\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right)U^{n+1}_{\sigma} \\ & & -M \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}}\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}-M\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}}\tau_{\sigma}dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}B\left(-\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right). \end{eqnarray*} By induction hypothesis, the first term is nonpositive. Moreover, using hypothesis (H7) and the property (\ref{propriB}), we obtain \begin{eqnarray*} \left(A^{n}\left(U^{n+1}-\textbf{M}\right)\right)_{K} &\leq &-M \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}}\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma} -M \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}}\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}\\ &\leq & -M \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}}\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}. \end{eqnarray*} However, using hypothesis (H6) and the definition of $q_{K,\sigma}$ (\ref{q}), we get \begin{equation*} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}}\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}=\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}}\int_{\sigma}q \cdot \mathbf{n}_{K,\sigma}\, ds= \int_{K}\text{div}(q)=0, \end{equation*} and then $\left(A^{n}\left(U^{n+1}-\textbf{M}\right)\right)_{K} \leq 0$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$.\\ So we have $A^{n}\left(U^{n+1}-\textbf{M}\right) \leq 0$, therefore we deduce that $U^{n+1}-\textbf{M} \leq 0$, hence $U^{n+1}_{K} \leq M \quad \forall K$ and we can show by the same way that $U^{n+1}_{K} \geq m \quad \forall K$.
nodes.statement_short: Write each step as a linear system with an M-matrix (column diagonally dominant), giving existence, uniqueness and positivity. The upper bound follows by induction, showing A^n(U^{n+1}-M) <= 0 using B(x)-B(-x)=-x and div q=0.

nodes.name: L-infinity bounds for the drift-diffusion system
nodes.statement: In the case of the drift-diffusion system for semiconductors, the hypothesis (H6) is not fulfilled ($ \Delta V \neq 0$). Nevertheless, if we assume that \begin{itemize} \item the doping profile $C$ is equal to $0$, \item there exist two constants $m>0$ and $M>0$ such that $m\leq \overline{N},N_{0},\overline{P},P_{0}\leq M$, \item $M \Delta t \leq 1$, \end{itemize} then we have, using the same kind of proof as in \cite{Chainais-Hillairet2003}, \begin{eqnarray*} 0 <m \leq N^{n}_{K} \leq M, & &\quad \forall K \in \mathcal{T}, \quad \forall n \geq 0,\\ 0 <m \leq P^{n}_{K} \leq M, & &\quad \forall K \in \mathcal{T}, \quad \forall n \geq 0. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: For zero doping, bounded data and M dt <= 1, the discrete densities N and P stay between m and M.

nodes.statement: Let $ \mathcal{D}$ be an admissible discretization of $ \Omega \times (0,T)$. The approximate solution to the problem (\ref{eq})-(\ref{CI})-(\ref{BCD})-(\ref{BCN}) associated to the discretization $\mathcal{D}$ is defined as piecewise constant function by: \begin{equation} u_{\delta}(x,t) = U^{n+1}_{K}, \quad \forall(x,t)\in K\times[t^{n},t^{n+1}[, \end{equation} where $ \lbrace U^{n}_{K},K \in \mathcal{T},0\leq n \leq N_{T}\rbrace $ is the unique solution to the scheme (\ref{CId})-(\ref{BCd})-(\ref{schemegene})-(\ref{flux}).

nodes.name: Discrete H^1 norm
nodes.statement: For a piecewise constant function $v_{\delta}$ defined by $v_{\delta}(x,t)=v_{K}^{n+1}$ for $(x,t) \in K \times [t^{n},t^{n+1}[$ and $v_{\delta}(\gamma,t)=v_{\sigma}^{n+1}$ for $(\gamma,t) \in \sigma \times [t^{n},t^{n+1}[$, we define \begin{equation*} \Vert v_{\delta} \Vert_{1,\mathcal{D}}^{2}=\sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}}\Delta t\left( \sum_{\substack{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int} \\ \sigma=K|L}} \tau_{\sigma} \left\vert v^{n+1}_{L}-v^{n+1}_{K}\right\vert^{2} + \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}}\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}} \tau_{\sigma} \left\vert v^{n+1}_{\sigma}-v^{n+1}_{K}\right\vert^{2} \right). \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Proof of the discrete L^2(0,T;H^1) estimate
nodes.statement: We follow the proof of Lemma 4.2 in \cite{Eymard2006}. Throughout this proof, $D_{i}$ denotes constants which depend only on $r$, $\textbf{q}$, $u_{0}$, $\overline{u}$, $\Omega$ and $T$. We set \begin{equation*} \overline{U}^{n+1}_{K}=\displaystyle{\frac{1}{\Delta t\text{m}(K)}\int_{t^{n}}^{t^{n+1}}\int_{K}\overline{u}(x,t)\, dx \, dt},\, \forall K \in \mathcal{T}, \,\ \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} w^{n+1}_{K}=U^{n+1}_{K}-\overline{U}^{n+1}_{K},\, \forall K \in \mathcal{T}, \,\ \forall n \in \mathbb{N}. \end{equation*} We multiply the scheme (\ref{schemegene}) by $\Delta t w^{n+1}_{K}$ and we sum over $n$ and $K$. We obtain $A+B=0$, where: \begin{eqnarray*} A &=& \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}}\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}}\text{m}(K)\left(U^{n+1}_{K}-U^{n}_{K}\right)w_{K}^{n+1},\\ B &=& \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma}w^{n+1}_{K}. \end{eqnarray*} \textbf{Estimate of $A$.} This term is treated in \cite{Eymard2006}. We get: \begin{equation} A \geq -\frac{1}{2}\Vert u_{0}-\overline{u}(.,0)\Vert_{L^{2}(\Omega)}^{2}-2\Vert \partial_{t}\overline{u}\Vert_{L^{1}(\Omega \times (0,T))}|M-m| =-D_{2}. \end{equation} \textbf{Estimate of $B$.} A discrete integration by parts yields (using that $w_{\sigma}^{n+1}=0$ for all $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext}^{D}$ and for all $n \geq 0$): \begin{equation*} B = \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{\substack{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int} \\ \sigma=K|L}} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma}\left(w^{n+1}_{K}-w_{L}^{n+1}\right) + \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma} \left(w^{n+1}_{K}-w_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right), \end{equation*} which delivers $B=B'-\overline{B}$, with: \begin{eqnarray*} B' &=& \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{\substack{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int} \\ \sigma=K|L}} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma}\left(U^{n+1}_{K}-U_{L}^{n+1}\right) + \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma}\left(U^{n+1}_{K}-U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right),\\ \overline{B} &=& \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{\substack{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int} \\ \sigma=K|L}} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma}\left(\overline{U}^{n+1}_{K}-\overline{U}_{L}^{n+1}\right) + \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma}\left(\overline{U}^{n+1}_{K}-\overline{U}_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right). \end{eqnarray*} \textbf{Estimate of $\overline{B}$.} Using the expression (\ref{flux2}) of $\mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}$, we have $\overline{B}=\overline{B}_{1}+\overline{B}_{2}$ with \begin{eqnarray*} \overline{B}_{1}&=& \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{\substack{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int} \\ \sigma=K|L}} \frac{\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}}{2}\left(U_{K}^{n+1}+U_{L}^{n+1}\right)\left(\overline{U}_{K}^{n+1}-\overline{U}_{L}^{n+1}\right) \\ & & + \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}}\frac{\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}}{2}\left(U_{K}^{n+1}+U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right)\left(\overline{U}_{K}^{n+1}-\overline{U}_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right),\\ \overline{B}_{2}&=& \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{\substack{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int} \\ \sigma=K|L}} \frac{\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}}{2}\coth\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right)\left(U_{K}^{n+1}-U_{L}^{n+1}\right)\left(\overline{U}_{K}^{n+1}-\overline{U}_{L}^{n+1}\right)\\ & & + \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}}\frac{\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}}{2}\coth\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right)\left(U_{K}^{n+1}-U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right)\left(\overline{U}_{K}^{n+1}-\overline{U}_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right). \end{eqnarray*} The term $\overline{B}_{1}$ is treated like in \cite{Eymard2006}, which leads to \begin{equation*} \vert \overline{B}_{1} \vert \leq M \Vert \textbf{q} \Vert_{\infty}\Vert \overline{u}_{\delta} \Vert_{1,\mathcal{D}}\text{dm}(\Omega)=D_{3}. \end{equation*} We apply Young's inequality for $\overline{B}_{2}$: for any $\alpha>0$, we have \begin{eqnarray*} \left\vert \overline{B}_{2} \right\vert &\leq &\frac{\alpha}{2} \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{\substack{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int} \\ \sigma=K|L}} \tau_{\sigma}\left(dr_{K,\sigma}^{n}\right)^{2}\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2dr_{K,\sigma}^{n}}\coth\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right)\right)^{2}\left(U_{K}^{n+1}-U_{L}^{n+1}\right)^{2}\\ & & + \frac{\alpha}{2} \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}} \tau_{\sigma}\left(dr_{K,\sigma}^{n}\right)^{2} \left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\coth\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right)\right)^{2}\left(U_{K}^{n+1}-U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right)^{2}\\ & &+ \frac{1}{2\alpha}\Vert \overline{u}_{\delta}\Vert_{1,\mathcal{D}}^{2}. \end{eqnarray*} By the hypothesis (H4), we have $\displaystyle{\inf_{s \in [m,M]}r'(s)>0}$. Then, using Lemma \ref{propdr}, the $L^{\infty}$ estimate on $u_{\delta}$ (\ref{estimlinf}) and the hypothesis (H5), we have \begin{equation*} \frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}} \leq \frac{\Vert \textbf{q} \Vert_{\infty}\text{diam}(\Omega)}{\displaystyle{\inf_{s\in [m,M]}r'(s)}}, \, \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\, \forall K \in \mathcal{T}, \, \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}. \end{equation*} Moreover, since $x \mapsto x \coth(x)$ is continuous on $\mathbb{R}$, we obtain \begin{equation*} \left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\coth\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right)\right)^{2} \leq D_{4}, \, \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\, \forall K \in \mathcal{T}, \, \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}. \end{equation*} Thus we can bound $ \overline{B}$: \begin{equation} \left\vert \overline{B} \right\vert \leq D_{3}+\frac{\alpha}{2}D_{4}\left(\sup_{s \in [m,M]}r'(s)\right)^{2}\Vert u_{\delta} \Vert_{1,\mathcal{D}}^{2}+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\Vert \overline{u}_{\delta} \Vert_{1,\mathcal{D}}. \end{equation} \textbf{Estimate of $B'$.} First, using the expression (\ref{flux2}) of the flux and Lemma \ref{propdr}, we have for all $n \geq 0$, for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$ and for all $\sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}$ \begin{eqnarray*} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma}\left(U^{n+1}_{K}-U^{n+1}_{L}\right) &=& \frac{\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}}{2}\left(\left(U_{K}^{n+1}\right)^{2}-\left(U^{n+1}_{L}\right)^{2}\right)\\ & & + \tau_{\sigma} r'(\eta_{K,\sigma}^{n})\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2r'(\eta_{K,\sigma}^{n})} \coth\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2r'(\eta_{K,\sigma}^{n})}\right)\left(U^{n+1}_{K}-U^{n+1}_{L}\right)^{2}. \end{eqnarray*} Then, since $x\coth(x) \geq 1$ for all $x\in \mathbb{R}$, we get: \begin{equation*} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma}\left(U^{n+1}_{K}-U^{n+1}_{L}\right) \geq \frac{\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}}{2}\left(\left(U_{K}^{n+1}\right)^{2}-\left(U^{n+1}_{L}\right)^{2}\right) + \tau_{\sigma}\inf_{s \in [m,M]}r'(s) \left(U^{n+1}_{K}-U^{n+1}_{L}\right)^{2}. \end{equation*} We obtain the same type of inequality for $\mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma}\left(U^{n+1}_{K}-U^{n+1}_{\sigma}\right)$. Thus we get \begin{eqnarray*} B' &\geq & \inf_{s \in [m,M]}r'(s)\Vert u_{\delta}\Vert_{1,\mathcal{D}}^{2}+\sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}}\Delta t\sum_{\substack{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int} \\ \sigma=K|L}} \frac{\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}}{2}\left(\left(U_{K}^{n+1}\right)^{2}-\left(U^{n+1}_{L}\right)^{2}\right)\\ & &+\sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}}\Delta t\sum_{K\in \mathcal{T}}\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}}\frac{\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}}{2}\left(\left(U_{K}^{n+1}\right)^{2}-\left(U^{n+1}_{\sigma}\right)^{2}\right). \end{eqnarray*} Through integrating by parts and using the hypothesis (H6), we get \begin{eqnarray*} & &\sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}}\Delta t\sum_{\substack{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int} \\ \sigma=K|L}} \frac{\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}}{2}\left(\left(U_{K}^{n+1}\right)^{2}-\left(U^{n+1}_{L}\right)^{2}\right)\\ &+&\sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}}\Delta t\sum_{K\in \mathcal{T}}\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}}\frac{\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}}{2}\left(\left(U_{K}^{n+1}\right)^{2}-\left(U^{n+1}_{\sigma}\right)^{2}\right) \\ & = & -\sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}}\Delta t \sum_{K\in \mathcal{T}}\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}} \frac{1}{2}\int_{\sigma}\textbf{q}(x)\cdot \textbf{n}_{K,\sigma}\, ds(x) \left(U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right)^{2}=-D_{5}, \end{eqnarray*} and then \begin{equation} B' \geq \inf_{s \in [m,M]}r'(s)\Vert u_{\delta}\Vert_{1,\mathcal{D}}^{2}-D_{5}. \end{equation} \textbf{Conclusion.} Using $A+B=0$ and estimates (\ref{estimA}), (\ref{estimBb}) and (\ref{estimBp}), we finally get for any $\alpha>0$: \begin{equation*} \left(\inf_{s\in [m,M]}r'(s)-\frac{\alpha}{2}D_{4}\left(\sup_{s\in [m,M]}r'(s)\right)^{2}\right)\Vert u_{\delta}\Vert_{1,\mathcal{D}}^{2} \leq D_{2}+D_{3}+D_{5}+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\Vert \overline{u}_{\delta}\Vert_{1,\mathcal{D}}^{2}, \end{equation*} thus for $\alpha < \displaystyle{\frac{2\displaystyle{\inf_{s\in [m,M]}r'(s)}}{D_{4}\left(\displaystyle{\sup_{s\in [m,M]}r'(s)}\right)^{2}}}$, we obtain $ \Vert u_{\delta} \Vert_{1,\mathcal{D}}^{2} \leq D_{1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Energy method following Eymard-Fuhrmann-Gaertner: test the scheme with U - Ubar and bound the terms. The key step uses x coth x >= 1 and Lemma on dr to get coercivity of B'.

nodes.name: Proof of the space and time translate estimates
nodes.statement: The following Lemma is a classical consequence of Proposition \ref{propestiml2} and estimates of time translation for $u_{\delta}$ obtained from the scheme (\ref{CId})-(\ref{BCd})-(\ref{schemegene})-(\ref{flux}). The proof is similar to those of Lemma 4.3 and Lemma 4.7 in \cite{Eymard2000}.
nodes.statement_short: By reference: consequence of the discrete H^1 estimate and time-translate estimates, as in Eymard-Gallouet-Herbin Lemmas 4.3 and 4.7.

nodes.name: Space and time translate estimates
nodes.statement: We suppose (H1)-(H7). Let $\mathcal{D}$ be an admissible discretization of $ \Omega \times (0,T)$. nodes.statement: \int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\left(\hat{u}_{\delta}(x,t+\tau)-\hat{u}_{\delta}(x,t)\right)^{2}\, dx \, dt \leq M_{2}|\tau|, \quad \forall \tau \in \mathbb{R}.

nodes.name: Dual mesh cells T_{K,sigma}
nodes.statement: For $K \in \mathcal{T}$ and $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}$, we define $T_{K,\sigma}$ as follows: \begin{itemize} \item if $\sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}$, then $T_{K,\sigma}$ is the cell whose vertices are $x_{K}$, $x_{L}$ and those of $\sigma=K|L$, \item if $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}$, then $T_{K,\sigma}$ is the cell whose vertices are $x_{K}$ and those of $\sigma$. \end{itemize}

nodes.name: Approximate gradient
nodes.statement: The approximation $\nabla^{\delta}u_{\delta}$ is a piecewise function defined in $\Omega \times (0,T)$ by: \begin{equation*} \nabla^{\delta}u_{\delta}(x,t)=\left\{\begin{array}{lcl} \displaystyle{\frac{\text{m}(\sigma)}{\text{m}(T_{K,\sigma})}\left(U^{n+1}_{L}-U^{n+1}_{K}\right) \mathbf{n}_{K,\sigma}} & & \text{ if } (x,t) \in T_{K,\sigma}\times [t^{n},t^{n+1}[, \,\ \sigma=K|L,\\ \displaystyle{\frac{\text{m}(\sigma)}{\text{m}(T_{K,\sigma})}\left(U^{n+1}_{\sigma}-U^{n+1}_{K}\right) \mathbf{n}_{K,\sigma}} & & \text{ if } (x,t) \in T_{K,\sigma}\times [t^{n},t^{n+1}[, \,\ \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}. \end{array}\right. \end{equation*}

nodes.statement: Using estimates (\ref{transspace})-(\ref{transtime}) and applying the Riesz-Fréchet-Kolmogorov criterion of strong compactness \cite{Brezis1983}, we obtain the first part of this Proposition. abla\psi(x,t)ight)\, dx \, dt\ & &+\int_{\Omega}u(x,0)\, \psi(x,0)\, dx=0, \end{eqnarray*} and then  egin{eqnarray*} & & \int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\left(u(x,t)\, \partial_{t}\psi(x,t)+
abla(r(u(x,t)))\cdot 
abla\psi(x,t)+u(x,t)\, \mathbf{q}(x)\cdot
